vulnerabilities.description: Telegram message handler passes raw event data without additional sanitization. The `event.from_user.id` check provides single-user access control, but there's no rate limiting on handler level to prevent brute-force or abuse.
ALLOWED_USER_ID parsed with `int()` from environment variable - will raise ValueError if .env contains non-integer. Consider adding validation with graceful fallback or explicit error message.

Open Interpreter execution environment uses ZAI_API_KEY which is a privileged key providing code execution capabilities. The interpreter runs with local Ollama models - ensure no untrusted input reaches the interpreter.

ALLOWED_SCREENPIP access control uses environment variable path checking - if ALLOWED_SCREENSHOT_DIRS is empty, any directory could be accessible. Verify the path validation covers all attack vectors.
Skills guard detects potential secret reads via regex patterns (`.env`, credentials) but this is audit-only - it logs warnings rather than blocking execution. Secrets could still be read.
Rate limiting is implemented with sliding window (30 req/min) which is good. Input sanitization via sanitizeTask function is present. No hardcoded secrets found - all API keys use process.env.
CORS properly configured with ALLOWED_ORIGINS. SQLite uses parameterized queries (db.run with ? placeholders). Input validation helpers present (isSafeIdent, sanitizeForSQL, validRoomName).

recommendations: Implement per-user rate limiting at the Telegram handler level to prevent abuse
Add input validation for ALLOWED_USER_ID with explicit error message when .env is misconfigured
Consider sandboxing Open Interpreter execution in a separate process with limited filesystem access
Implement secret blocking in skills_guard.py to actually prevent reading .env files rather than just logging
Add comprehensive audit logging for all API key access attempts
Implement CSRF protection for web endpoints if session authentication is added in future
Add dependency vulnerability scanning to CI pipeline (trivy, safety, or pip-audit)
Consider implementing TPM or hardware key storage for API keys in production
